newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Yen in spotlight on Hungary FX futures market.
newsitem.headline: Yen in spotlight on Hungary FX futures market.

text.p: Easing yen futures were the most popular on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) on Monday but other currencies that lost against the dollar were also actively traded, dealers said.
"The yen, Swiss franc and mark all weakened against the dollar," said Janos Mladenszki of Futures Broker.
December was the most popular maturity, accounting for more than two-thirds of Monday's turnover in contract terms.
However, futures did not move exactly in line with spot prices, Mlandeszki said.
"Position closings gave some support to currency futures prices," he said.
The day's favourite, the yen, finished lower for September at 155.76 forints, down 0.04. It also went 15 fillers down for December to 162.43 and eased five fillers for March to 167.25.
The second most popular currency, the mark, went lower for June, September and December by 15 to 40 fillers.
Dollar futures registered the most significant changes ending at 183.20 forints for July, up 1.50, 189 for September, up 1.70 and rose 1.8 forints for December to 195.
Total BCE trade was a below-average 5.28 billion forints, or 36,382 contracts, with yens accounting for 13,432 lots, marks for 8,700 and Swiss franc for 7,760.
The Budapest Stock Exchange's currency futures market showed the first signs of life after five tradeless days with 30 contracts for December marks.
